Backend: 20/20 pytest tests PASS covering invoice-review CRUD, review-summary shape + proration, MPCA-signed-pdf endpoint, approve gates (missing reviews / missing PDF / sum-of-accepted overrides action payload), and Phase E invoice CRUD locks (create/patch/delete → 409; unlocks on Rejected). Frontend: verified /reimbursement-claims/{cid}/division-form and /mpca-review-form routes render with correct data-testids, letterheads (Indore Division vs MPCA), addressee, 5-bullet declaration, sections A/B, logo (2 images), and MpcaLineItemReviewPanel correctly hidden for Draft claims.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/reimbursement_claims.py::approve_claim — line 723 the eligible-cap check `approved > eligible and not invoice_reviews` uses only summary.eligible_total_inr; when a claim has reviews the code assumes sum-of-accepted is authoritative and skips the eligible cap. That's intentional per spec but note: nothing bounds the sum of accepted amounts against the tournament budget total. If MPCA accidentally accepts more than the approved budget ceiling, we approve it. Consider a soft warning/hard cap.
routes/reimbursement_claims.py::set_invoice_review — 422 message uses `payload.accepted_inr` as raw float; if a user sends '9e10' it will print in scientific notation. Cosmetic.

routes/tournament_invoices.py Phase E lock query filters by status Submitted/Under_Review/Approved. Consolidator flow (District→Division) doesn't set route_to_body_id='MPCA' but Phase E lock is body_id+tournament_id based only — good — it will lock invoices under a District claim too, which may or may not be desired. Confirm with product.

get_review_summary proration uses `sum(allocations.amount_inr)` as denominator falling back to 1.0 — but if invoice has allocs summing to 0 the proration divides by 1 producing wrong per-head numbers. Edge case, not blocking.
MpcaClaimReviewForm.jsx renders letterhead 'A.' / 'B.' but not 'Section A/B' literal — spec used 'Section A' / 'Section B' wording; harmless labeling divergence.
DivisionReimbursementClaimForm renders signature blocks (Hon. Secretary / Treasurer / President) via SigBlock component — verified present in JSX (lines 187-189).
